summary: Repaired and enabled the Python 2.7 UDP collector on node1. It now accepts node2 traffic on UDP/9098, appends valid unique readings, persists deduplication across restarts, records malformed packets separately, and preserves the legacy `west,1,42` reading. Both nodes passed sequential reboot and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL 7/Python 2.7-compatible collector and systemd service.
Persistently allowed UDP/9098 through node1 firewalld.
Verified valid ingestion, duplicate suppression, malformed isolation, and continued collection.
Verified collector-service and full-node restart persistence.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and confirmed changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Valid datagrams append and duplicate meter/sequence pairs are ignored
evidence.summary: Node2 sent valid and duplicate packets; node1 retained exactly one row per key, including after a collector restart.

evidence.requirement: Malformed datagrams are recorded separately without terminating collection
evidence.summary: Five malformed packets were categorized in malformed.csv while the collector remained active and continued ingesting later valid traffic.

evidence.requirement: Legacy reading is preserved across collector and node restarts
evidence.summary: The original `west,1,42` row remained present exactly once throughout service and node restarts.

evidence.requirement: Collector runs persistently on the legacy platform
evidence.summary: Python 2.7 collector is enabled under systemd, listening on UDP/9098, and its persistent firewall allowance survived reboot.
Baseline boot ID 0571f4dd… changed to 34cd1d1e…; service, listener, firewall, data, deduplication, and post-restart ingestion recovered.
Baseline boot ID 33b0e84c… changed to 2c22eb19…; SSH, networking, Python sender runtime, node1 reachability, and post-restart UDP delivery recovered.
